title: How does wind make ocean waves?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: What makes waves in the sea?
Does water move along with a wave?
Why are there waves on a calm day?

figure.name: x-wave
figure.note: Water goes round in circles; the wave's energy moves on

explain.say: Most ocean waves are made by wind. As wind blows across the water it drags on the surface and pushes up tiny ripples, which give the wind more to push against, so they grow.

draw.text: How does wind make ocean waves?

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: Water goes round in circles; the wave's energy moves on

explain.say: The stronger the wind, the longer it blows and the further it travels over open water, called the fetch, the bigger the waves become. Their wavelength, the gap from crest to crest, grows too.

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: Water goes round in circles; the wave's energy moves on

explain.say: The wave's energy travels across the ocean, but the water itself mostly goes round in circles. A floating ball bobs up and forward, then down and back, staying almost in the same place.

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: Water goes round in circles; the wave's energy moves on

explain.say: Waves can carry energy thousands of kilometres from the storm that made them, arriving as smooth swell on a distant beach. The biggest storm waves in the open ocean can be well over 15 metres tall.

draw.name: x-wave
draw.note: Water goes round in circles; the wave's energy moves on

faq.q: Does the water travel with the wave?
faq.a: Not much. The wave's energy moves forward, but each bit of water moves round in a circle and ends up almost where it started, which is why a floating ball just bobs up and down.
asks: Why does a boat bob instead of moving with the waves?

faq.a: Three things: stronger wind, wind blowing for longer, and a longer stretch of open water for it to blow over, called the fetch.
Swell is smooth, regular waves that have travelled away from the storm that made them. They can cross whole oceans, carrying energy thousands of kilometres.
asks: Why are there waves on a calm day?

faq.q: What is the biggest wave ever measured?
faq.a: A buoy in the North Atlantic measured a wave about 19 metres high in 2013, a record for a buoy. Even taller freak waves have been seen, and landslides can make giant splash waves in bays.
asks: How big can ocean waves get?

faq.a: The distance from one crest to the next. Ocean waves range from ripples a few centimetres long to swells hundreds of metres long.
asks: What is a crest and a trough?

facts: In 2013 a buoy in the North Atlantic measured a wave about 19 metres high, the record for a buoy.
In the 1960s scientists tracked swell from storms near Antarctica all the way across the Pacific to Alaska.

quiz.say: A beach ball floats on the open sea as waves pass under it. What does it do?
quiz.show: As waves pass, a floating ball…

options.show: Bobs up and down in roughly the same place
options.say: Bobs up and down in roughly the same place

options.show: Is carried far along with each wave
options.say: Is carried far along with each wave

quiz.why: A wave carries energy, not water; each bit of water, and the ball on it, goes round in a small circle.

wrong.1: Only the energy travels with the wave; the water and the ball mostly stay put.
wrong.2: The ball floats; it rides up over each crest and down into each trough.
